title: Carbide‐Derived Carbons: Effect of Pore Size on Hydrogen Uptake and Heat of Adsorption
material_description: TiC-CDC | carbide-derived carbon made by chlorinating TiC powder (Alfa Aesar, ca. 2-4 um) in Cl2 for 3 h at 800 °C, as-produced (not H2-annealed); NLDFT average pore size 0.92 nm
purification_method: cooled under Ar flow to remove residual metal chlorides
source_location: main-4.png (p. 2291), Figure 7, series TiC-CDC (filled squares)
notes: archive: fig7_TiC-CDC.json. Digitized 18.333 mmHg (x 0.00133322 bar/mmHg), 0.6598 wt%. partially overlapped marker near origin; centre from the 6x6-px all-dark core of a 7x7-px dark block. Temperature printed as -196 °C. Paper names no uptake basis (uptake_type unspecified); volumetric Autosorb-1, so basis_inferred = excess by instrumental default. wt% convention stated in Experimental: wt% = rho_H2 * v_H2 * 100 per unit mass of sorbent, explicitly not normalized by sorbent+adsorbate mass (W1). Average pore size 0.92 nm is the weighted average (Eq. 2) of the NLDFT PSD from Ar sorption at -196 °C, printed in Fig. 3 TiC CDC 800 °C panel (main-3.png). isotherm_point_count 22 is a lower bound: further markers near the origin (P < ~15 mmHg, < ~0.4 wt%) overlap those of the other two series and cannot be separated (log.md). Reconciled by agent C: point digitized by B only (B row HYC-0121-M1); A merged it with a neighbouring marker and dropped it. Uncertainty = 1% of the 0-3.5 wt% axis span. Sample-level fields harmonized with the reconciled sample (purification_method as on the matched rows).
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
